chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from his father, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: I heard my father narrating from his father (peace be upon them both). He said:

The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said: There is not a prayer whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before the people: Go to the fires that you have kindled on your backs and extinguish them with your prayer.

key_terms.صلاة: Prayer; the ritual worship performed five times daily in Islam
key_terms.ملك: Angel; a celestial being that calls people to prayer
key_terms.نيران: Fires; metaphor for sins and their consequences

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about how prayer extinguishes sins?
ai.summary: Through a chain reaching the Prophet (SAWW) via Imams al-Sadiq and al-Baqir, this hadith presents a vivid metaphorical image: each time a prayer is due, an angel calls upon people to go and extinguish the fires they have built on their own backs through their sins. The prayer is thus depicted as the means of extinguishing these sins. This powerful imagery was used in early Muslim communities to encourage timely observance of the five daily prayers, emphasizing that accumulated sins weigh upon a person like fire on the back, and that prayer is the divinely appointed remedy.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from his father from `Abdullah b. `Abdullah al-Dahqan from Wasil b. Sulayman from `Abdullah b. Sinan from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said: I heard my father narrate from his father (as).  He said:

The Prophet (s) said: There is not a prayer that is attended on time except that an angel calls out from before the people: “Go to the fire that you have lit on your backs and extinguish it with your prayer.”
